claims.text: Annealing the APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating at 550 °C produces a refined grain structure.
Annealing the coating at 550 °C produces a denser coating structure.
The annealed coating rapidly forms stable Al-rich passive oxide or hydroxide layers.
The annealed coating rapidly forms stable Cr-rich passive oxide or hydroxide layers.
The passive layers enhance corrosion resistance relative to uncoated and as-sprayed SS316L.
The feedstock is an equiatomic, single-phase BCC AlCoCrFeNi powder with spherical particles 20–25 µm in size.
Annealing at 550 °C produces an average grain size of 15 µm.
Annealing at 550 °C increases the fraction of low-angle grain boundaries.
Annealing at 550 °C minimizes voids in the coating.
The annealed coating retains a dominant BCC phase with minor FCC phases.
Corrosion produces passive layers that include Cr2O3, Fe(OH)3, Cr(OH)3, and Co(OH)2.
Grain refinement increases coating hardness and impedes dislocation motion.
High-entropy and sluggish-diffusion effects facilitate rapid formation of protective passive oxides.
The refined structure and protective oxides inhibit pit and crack propagation.
The proposed mechanisms reduce susceptibility to sulphide attack in aggressive chemical environments and high-temperature molten salts.
The 550 °C annealed coating will have higher microhardness than both uncoated SS316L and the as-sprayed coating.
The 550 °C annealed coating will have lower corrosion current and higher polarization resistance than both baselines.
The 550 °C annealed coating will show less hot-corrosion weight gain than both baselines.
Annealing above 550 °C causes grain growth and softening that reduce the beneficial properties.
The hypothesis is expected to apply only within the specified APS, annealing, sulfuric-acid, and cyclic molten-salt exposure conditions, while behavior outside those conditions remains uncertain.
